item.text:
I've now covered all remaining source files (`commands.go` is only RPC struct definitions; `future.go` is standard future/`deferError` plumbing) and confirmed there is no further productive automated avenue (only `v1.7.3` is cached — no newer version to diff as a bug oracle; no fuzz targets; nested modules unbuildable offline).

No new defect surfaced. Rather than invent findings, I'll keep the conclusion evidence-based.

Final status of the audit:

- **Supplied implementation:** unmodified upstream `github.com/hashicorp/raft v1.7.3` (proven byte-for-byte three ways). No injected defect in the graded module.
- **Consensus correctness:** no concrete defect demonstrated — the entire package passes in six full runs and under `-race`; every review surface (election/pre-vote, replication/pipelining, commitment/quorum, configuration changes, snapshots/restore, log cache, transport, futures) matches documented upstream behavior.
- **One confirmed, reproducible defect:** C1, in the shipped *test helper* `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` (`testing.go:691`) — it samples `rafts[0]`'s configuration once and never refreshes it, so a transient lag becomes a guaranteed 5s spurious failure (~18/100 runs of `TestRaft_HasExistingState`); re-sampling inside the retry loop fixes it (100/100). This is a test-utility bug, not a consensus-correctness bug, and I've kept the fix in scratch (`work/diag/`) distinct from the captured source.
- **Scope limits recorded:** nested `fuzzy/`/`raft-compat/` modules are outside the graded package and cannot run offline.

Everything is preserved in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-11_16-25-33-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md) with commands, retained execution IDs, and the repro/fix. The audit is complete; I don't see a further investigation that would add signal beyond what's already documented.
